collections.name: Blue Heron Bridge

collections.name: Cozumel

products.title: Frogfish, Waiting
products.story: A frogfish doing what frogfish do best — being a sponge until something swims too close. Shot at Blue Heron Bridge, Florida.

products.title: Banded Coral Shrimp
products.story: Candy-striped and fearless — this cleaner shrimp ran its station on a Roatán reef, gloved claws out.

products.title: Spotted Drum
products.story: The reef's restless dancer. Juvenile spotted drums never stop moving, which makes a sharp frame a small victory.

products.title: Spiny Lobster
products.story: Antennae first, questions later. A Florida spiny lobster meets the dome port head-on.

products.title: Orange Cup Coral
products.story: Cup corals open like fireworks after dark — a night-dive bloom in full orange.

products.title: Crinoid in Bloom
products.story: A feather star unfurled against the dark — the ocean's oldest flower that isn't a flower at all.

products.title: Filefish Pair
products.story: Two whitespotted filefish keeping formation over a Cozumel reef — an easy shot to see, a hard one to time.

products.title: Trumpetfish
products.story: Vertical, patient, and pretending very hard to be a stick of gorgonian. It fooled the reef, not the camera.

copy.aboutTeaser: I'm Devyn — a macro photographer who spends as much time as possible below the surface. My favorite subjects are the small ones: shrimp the size of a fingernail, frogfish pretending to be sponges, and everything else most divers swim past.
copy.aboutLong: What started as a way to remember dives became the reason for them. I shoot macro — the tiny, strange, spectacular life that hides on every reef and under every pier piling. My home water is Blue Heron Bridge in Florida, one of the best small-critter dive sites anywhere, and my logbook keeps pulling me back to the Caribbean: Cozumel's walls, Roatán's reefs, and wherever the next small thing is hiding.
